new_upstream_defects: AppModel.swift:638 vs :642 — forwardThread appends the new thread to `threads` (:638), expands its project (:639) and records it as the last project (:640) BEFORE awaiting installContinuation, then returns nil on failure (:642) without removing it. Realistic worst outcome: after a forward whose continuation fails to install, an empty thread titled "Continued: <source title>" is left in the sidebar, unselected and unexplained; the next scheduleSave from any other cause persists it. No data is lost and nothing is overwritten, so this is a stray-record defect, not a destructive one. Specified as written in PR-LAUNCH-082 rather than repaired.

AttachmentPreview.swift:82 — `PreviewImages.attachments` is an unbounded `[String: Attachment]` keyed by path with no eviction, in direct contrast to `FileIcons` twenty lines below it (:112-125), which is explicitly bounded at 64 with a comment saying why ("Bounded: icons are small but unbounded kinds are not"). Realistic worst outcome: a long session that previews many distinct images grows the map without limit. The records are three small strings each, so the growth is slow and this is a minor leak rather than a user-visible failure; the per-path identity it provides is load-bearing (the preview panel's toggle compares it), so it cannot simply be dropped. Recorded in PR-COMPOSER-206 as unbounded.

AttachmentPreview.swift:217-221 (latent) — `AttachmentVideoThumbnail`'s `.task(id: attachment.path)` opens with `guard image == nil else { return }`, so a view instance rebound to a different path keeps the previous video's frame on screen. The photo path handles the same case correctly: TimelineRows.swift:1346-1355 re-resolves the memoized image for the NEW path and assigns it. I could not demonstrate a reachable failure: all three call sites (ComposerView.swift:1001, EditorAttachments.swift:22, TimelineRows.swift:1229) use `ForEach(attachments)` keyed by Attachment's own Identifiable id, so a different attachment gets fresh @State. Reporting it as a latent inconsistency, not a confirmed defect, so it is on record if a future strip is keyed by index or if an Attachment's path can change under a stable id.
